Surviving unchanged: masthead with small glyph + name, pale ground, white 4 px bordered cards with a square thumbnail tile, single green accent on the filled button and availability chip, calendar of white boxes, radio session cards. The render matches the default on every identity-carrying element (ground, card, type voice, accent, chips); it avoids the opposite but puts nothing of its own in place.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same placeholder wrench tile instead of the tool
findings.description: All ten cards on the find page carry an identical pale-green square with a wrench outline where a thumbnail belongs. It reads as a placeholder, makes the grid uniform, and gives members nothing to recognise ('the drill with two batteries') at a glance.
findings.impact: Members may have to read every title to tell a drill from a sander, and the page is likely to look unfinished to first-time visitors.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail is for: either real photos of the library's own tools (the stock is one of each, so each photo is the actual item) or remove the slot; do not ship an identical tile per card.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar covers part of the pick-up calendar
findings.description: In every tool-page capture the white sticky action bar sits across the calendar, hiding the week of 11-17 October and cutting the 'Open' tag of Saturday 10. It may be partly a full-page capture artefact of a fixed bar, but no bottom padding is visible to let the last rows scroll clear of it.
findings.impact: The day a member most likely wants (the coming Saturday) may sit under the bar on phones, and the page looks broken.
findings.recommendation: Reserve space under the content equal to the bar so every calendar row can scroll clear; verify with a viewport-only capture.

findings.title: Basket session cards break into one full-width card and five squeezed ones
findings.description: At 1280 the first session (Wednesday 28 October) spans the full width while the other five share one row and wrap to three lines each ('Saturday 24 / October, 10:00 to / 13:00'). Sessions are also listed latest-first, so the soonest session is last.
findings.impact: Members may read the full-width card as recommended or default, and the soonest session (usually the one they want) is the hardest to find.
findings.recommendation: Decide one layout for the session list that gives every session equal weight and one-line dates, ordered by date as members think of it.

findings.title: Tool details list uses two different label column widths
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from align values at one x position; Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case align at another, so the value column steps left halfway down the list.
findings.impact: Weakens the 'careful' attribute on the page where members compare specs; looks like two lists pasted together.
findings.recommendation: Treat the details as one list with one label column, or separate the two groups with a heading so the change is intentional.

findings.title: No-results state shows the full tool list
findings.description: With 'sewing machine' in the search field, the captured no-results state shows all ten tools and no message, identical to the default state.
findings.impact: A member may believe the library has a sewing machine among the listed tools, or that search did nothing.

evidence.detail: query visible, list unchanged, no empty-state copy

findings.recommendation: Design an empty state in the desk volunteer's voice; confirm whether the capture ran before the search was submitted.

findings.title: Filter panel uses unthemed native date and select controls on mismatched baselines
findings.description: The open filter panel shows a native date input with 'yyyy/mm/dd' and the platform calendar glyph, and a native select; the 'Category' label sits about 30 px lower than 'Available from'.
findings.impact: The date format contradicts the declared 'Saturday 17 October' format members use, and the panel looks unfinished next to the styled search row.
findings.recommendation: Bring the filter controls into the same component set as the search row, align labels on one baseline, and present the date in the declared format.

findings.title: Dark theme drops the chip background only on 'available' badges
findings.description: In dark mode the green 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' badges have no tinted background while the grey 'later' badges keep theirs, inverting the light theme's emphasis.
findings.impact: Members in dark mode (common in the use scene) may read the later-availability tools as the highlighted ones.
findings.recommendation: Give the badge-available component a visible dark-theme surface so both badge kinds keep their light-theme relationship.

findings.title: On phones the search field sits below all ten tools and names truncate
findings.description: At 375 the find page lists all cards first and the search field and filter after them, near the footer; tool names are cut with an ellipsis ('Cordless drill 18 V, co…'), hiding exactly the distinguishing words ('two batteries' vs 'one battery'). Nav items also wrap to two lines.
findings.impact: Phone users (the majority) may scroll past ten cards to search, and cannot tell the two drills apart from the list.
findings.recommendation: Keep the same order at every width and let tool names wrap.

findings.title: No identity beyond the name in body text; the membership-card green has no visible source
findings.description: Across all five surfaces the only identity is 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body text beside a small stock wrench icon. DESIGN.md says the green comes from the membership card, but nothing in the render shows the card, the room or the desk, so the colour reads as a category default.
findings.impact: Members may not recognise this as their library's own service, and 'neighbourly' is carried only by the copy.
findings.recommendation: Decide one identity floor that comes from the library's own world and carries 'neighbourly, not folksy' (for example a designed name, or the membership card's reasoning made visible) and one signature tied to the session mechanism; keep the Operate structure.

strengths: Copy in the desk volunteer's voice: concrete, brief, explains deposit and sessions at each step.
One filled primary per page and a calm restrained palette; dark theme composed rather than inverted, with legible error states.
keep: Keep the session-marking on the calendar and the deposit on every card; any identity work must not dilute the plain, concrete voice.
not_assessable: Motion (toast fade, button colour transitions), focus rings and hover states cannot be judged from stills.
Whether the sticky bar overlap exists in a live viewport or only in full-page capture.
